Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestInternationalFixedChronology_test_InternationalFixedDate_from_LocalDate.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestInternationalFixedChronology/TestInternationalFixedChronology_test_InternationalFixedDate_from_LocalDate.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The test only actually uses `data_samples()` and the single parameterized method — all the other `data_*` methods (and most imports) are dead code that severely hurts readability. Let me verify the CUT API before refactoring.The CUT API checks out. Now I'll write the improved test — removing the large blocks of dead, unused data methods and unused imports, keeping only what the single parameterized test actually exercises, and formatting the sample data legibly.Now let me compile-check the result.Compiles cleanly (`COMPILE_OK`). 

I improved understandability while preserving runtime behavior exactly — the same `InternationalFixedDate.from(iso)` assertions over the identical sample pairs. Changes:

- **Removed dead code**: the original carried 14 unused `data_*` methods (badDates, lengthOfMonth, ranges, getLong, with, plus, until, etc.) and ~40 unused imports — none referenced by the single parameterized test. They were pure noise.
- **Reformatted the sample data**: one date pair per line with comments grouping them by intent (year boundaries, Leap Day, Year Day, leap vs. non-leap century years, historical/modern dates).
- **Added documentation** explaining what the test verifies and the calendar concepts (Leap Day, Year Day) behind the samples.
